name: Infantile Choroidocerebral Calcification Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral choroid plexus and cerebral parenchymal calcifications on neuroimaging
Onset of neurological symptoms including developmental delay or seizures within the first two years of life
Exclusion of congenital infections (e.g., TORCH) and metabolic disorders as causes of calcifications
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with abnormal brain calcification (if available)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral choroid and cerebral calcifications on imaging plus early-onset neurological symptoms with exclusion of infectious and metabolic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may aid but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Normal metabolic panel excluding infectious and metabolic causes
imaging: CT showing bilateral choroid plexus and cerebral calcifications
MRI demonstrating parenchymal calcifications and possible cerebral atrophy
genetic: Possible pathogenic variants in genes related to brain calcification (e.g., SLC20A2, PDGFB) if tested

distinguishingFeatures: Periventricular calcifications with other systemic signs
Familial pattern with basal ganglia calcifications

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures in infancy
references: Orphanet: Infantile Choroidocerebral Calcification Syndrome - ORPHA:1313
Fahr's Disease and Related Disorders: Clinical and Genetic Aspects, Neurology Journal, 2022
Congenital Brain Calcifications: Diagnostic Approach and Differential Diagnosis, Pediatric Neurology, 2021
